Is spironolactone a blood thinner?
:
No.
Spironolactone is not a blood thinner.
It does not affect blood clotting.
It is not used to prevent clots or strokes.
Warfarin, apixaban, or aspirin are used to prevent clots or strokes.
It is a diuretic that lowers blood pressure and reduces fluid build-up.
Spironolactone does interact with some blood thinners indirectly.
Heparin and low molecular weight heparin can raise potassium.
Taking them with spironolactone increases the risk of a high potassium level.
Can I stop taking spironolactone suddenly?
:
Spironolactone does not cause withdrawal symptoms.
Spironolactone does not need to be tapered the way a steroid does.
Even so, do not stop it without speaking to your doctor.
Stopping it can allow fluid to build up again.
Stopping it can allow your blood pressure to rise.
Stopping it can allow your heart failure to worsen.
